formation.title: The Consolidation of Hanover
formation.text:
The scattered Brunswick-Luneburg principalities are united under a single Welf banner. The question before us is not merely one of governance, but of orientation. To the west lies Britain, where our dynasty may one day wear a second crown: an alliance that would bring naval power, trade wealth, and military subsidies, but also entanglement in wars far from our borders. To the south lies the Empire, where Gottingen's scholars are forging new ideas and the Harz mines still yield silver: a path of self-reliance, intellectual ambition, and German identity.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Look to the sea: our dynasty's future lies with Britain

modifiers.name: The Hanoverian Succession
modifiers.text: The Act of Settlement binds our dynasty to the British crown, opening channels of trade, subsidy, and shared military obligation across the North Sea.

options.text: Look to Gottingen. We shall be a light of learning

modifiers.name: The Welf Renaissance
modifiers.text: The House of Welf charts its own course, investing in universities, scientific inquiry, and the arts to build a beacon of Enlightenment thought in northern Germany.

advances.name: Welf Dynasty
advances.text: The House of Welf is among the oldest princely dynasties in Europe, tracing its lineage through centuries of imperial politics.

advances.name: Harz Silver Mining
advances.text: The silver mines of the Harz Mountains have enriched the Welf dukes for generations, funding their courts and armies.

advances.name: Sachsenspiegel Tradition
advances.text: The Sachsenspiegel, composed around 1220, codified Saxon customary law and became the foundation of legal practice across northern Germany.

advances.name: Lower Saxon Trade
advances.text: The market towns of Hildesheim, Braunschweig, and Hanover sit at the crossroads of north German trade routes linking the Hanse cities to the interior.

advances.name: Marstall of Celle
advances.text: The dukes of Lüneburg leave their old city for Celle in 1378 and make the castle on the Aller their court. Beside it stands the ducal Marstall, where the riding and war horses of the household are kept and bred from the hardy stock of the heath.

advances.name: Calenberg Ascendancy
advances.text: The Principality of Calenberg consolidates power among the competing Brunswick branches, centralizing administration under a single Welf ruler.

advances.name: The Ducal Residences
advances.text: Shut out of the city of Brunswick by its burghers, the dukes make Wolfenbüttel their seat in 1432, as the Lüneburg line made Celle before them. Moated castles are rebuilt as courts, with a chapel, a chancery and a hall for the painters and singers the duke keeps.

advances.name: Oberharzer Wasserregal
advances.text: An engineering marvel of 107 dams, 310 km of ditches, and dozens of water wheels: the Wasserregal powers the Harz mines through ingenious hydraulic management.

advances.name: Academia Julia
advances.text:
Duke Julius of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel founds a university at Helmstedt in 1576, the Academia Julia, and gives his pits the same care as his scholars. The deep adit at the Rammelsberg that bears his name, begun generations before him, is driven through in 1585 and drains workings that had stood under water since about 1300.

Available in: Oberharzer Bergwerk

advances.name: The Emperor's Rescuer
advances.text: At Wenzenbach near Regensburg in 1504, Duke Eric of Calenberg saves the life of King Maximilian in the press of battle and is knighted on the field. The Welfs stand high in the favour of the house of Austria.

event.title: The Emperor's Rescuer
event.text: In the war over the Landshut inheritance, King Maximilian has been dragged from his horse among the Bohemian foot at Wenzenbach. Duke Eric of Calenberg has cut his way to him and brought him out alive, wounded himself in the doing. Maximilian has knighted the duke on the field and named him a friend of his house. We may use this favour to amplify our standing among the courts of the Empire, or we may double down on the military service that earned us this honor, cementing our reputation as indispensable defenders of the Empire.

options.text: Our voice shall carry weight in every court

modifiers.name: Imperial Favour
modifiers.text: The man who saved the Emperor is heard with respect in every court of the Empire.

options.text: The Empire needs our swords more than our words

modifiers.name: Imperial Service
modifiers.text: Our troops are the shield of the Empire: the Emperor rewards those who answer his call.

advances.name: Welf Reisige
advances.text: The Welf dukes of the sixteenth century ride to war at the head of their Reisige: armoured horsemen of the ducal household and of the knightly families of Calenberg and Wolfenbüttel.

advances.name: Lower Saxon Circle Director
advances.text: As director of the Lower Saxon Imperial Circle, Hanover bears responsibility for mustering the Circle's defense levies and protecting the region against external threats.

advances.name: The Ninth Electorate
advances.text: In 1692 Emperor Leopold I raises Duke Ernest Augustus to prince-elector: a ninth seat in the college that chooses the Emperor. His wife Sophia, granddaughter of James I, carries a claim to the English throne, which Parliament confirms to her and her heirs in 1701.

advances.name: Subsidy Troops
advances.text: The Welf dukes hire out their well-trained soldiers to Venice, France, Spain, England, and the Emperor, turning military manpower into diplomatic currency.

advances.name: Lauenburg and the Elbe
advances.text: When the last duke of Saxe-Lauenburg dies in 1689, George William of Celle occupies the duchy. The Welfs now hold the Elbe crossing at Lauenburg, its toll, and the old salt road and canal to Lübeck and the Baltic.

advances.name: The Helmstedt School
advances.text: From 1635 the Academia Julia at Helmstedt is the common university of all the Welf lines. Georg Calixtus teaches there that the divided churches can be reconciled, and Hermann Conring founds the study of German legal history.

event.title: The Scholars of Helmstedt
event.text: While the Empire tears itself apart over confession, the Welf university at Helmstedt goes its own way. Georg Calixtus, professor of theology since 1614, teaches that Lutherans, Reformed and Catholics share the faith of the first five centuries and may be reconciled upon it. The orthodox of Wittenberg denounce him as a mixer of religions; the dukes keep him in his chair. Beside him Hermann Conring lectures on medicine, on politics and on the true origins of German law. Students come from every Protestant land of the north, and the councillors of the Welf courts are trained in a school that prefers argument to anathema.

options.text: Let knowledge flourish in the halls of Helmstedt

modifiers.name: The Helmstedt School
modifiers.text: Helmstedt's moderate theology and its learned jurists draw students from across the Protestant north.

advances.name: Hanoverian Military Reform
advances.text: The Hanoverian army is reorganized into a professional standing force, trained to the standards demanded by its commitments to both the Empire and the British crown.

advances.name: Legacy of Minden
advances.text: At Minden in 1759, Hanoverian infantry advanced in open formation against French cavalry and broke them with disciplined volley fire: a triumph of training over tradition.

event.title: The Miracle at Minden
event.text: On the morning of August 1, 1759, six British and two Hanoverian infantry battalions advance in line formation across an open plain against massed French cavalry near the town of Minden. Against all doctrine and expectation, their disciplined volley fire shatters charge after charge. By afternoon, Marshal Contades's army is in retreat. The Battle of Minden proves that well-drilled infantry, holding their nerve and their formation, can defeat the most fearsome cavalry in Europe. The Hanoverian soldiers who stood at Minden have etched their courage into military history.

options.text: Press the advantage. Carry the fight to the enemy

modifiers.name: Minden Discipline
modifiers.text: The lesson of Minden: disciplined fire wins battles. Press the advantage while the enemy reels.

options.text: Hold the line: our strength is in our steadfastness

modifiers.name: Minden Steadfastness
modifiers.text: The lesson of Minden: hold your ground and let the enemy break upon your line.

advances.name: The Pragmatic Army
advances.text: In 1743 sixteen thousand Hanoverians march to the Main with the British and Austrians, and at Dettingen the Elector-King leads them in person against the French. The red-coated foot of the electorate proves itself the equal of any in Europe.

event.title: The King at Dettingen
event.text: On 27 June 1743 the allied army of British, Hanoverians and Austrians is caught on the bank of the Main near Dettingen, with the French across its road and French guns firing from over the river. George II, Elector of Hanover and King of Great Britain, dismounts, draws his sword and leads the foot forward himself. The French household cavalry charges and breaks on the steady fire of the line; by evening the French are driven back across the river with heavy loss. No king of Great Britain will lead an army in battle again, and the Hanoverian regiments that stood beside him that day will carry the name of Dettingen with pride.

options.text: Their steadiness shall never be forgotten

modifiers.name: Pride of Dettingen
modifiers.text: The Hanoverian foot that stood under the eye of its Elector at Dettingen has earned a reputation as the finest German infantry in Europe.

advances.name: Gottingen School
advances.text: In 1734 the Elector founds the Georgia Augusta at Gottingen, with an open library and no confessional oath. There Schlozer and his colleagues pioneer modern historiography, statistical analysis, and comparative politics, transforming how Europeans understand their own past.

advances.name: British Subsidies
advances.text: Britain subsidizes the defense of Hanover with hundreds of thousands of pounds annually, funding fortifications, garrisons, and the army that guards the electorate.

advances.name: Hanoverian Jager
advances.text: Recruited from the foresters and gamekeepers of Lower Saxony, Hanoverian Jager fight as light infantry, expert marksmen trained to exploit wooded and broken terrain. When the French occupy the electorate in 1803 many cross to Britain and serve in the light battalions of the King's German Legion.

advances.name: Kingdom of Hanover
advances.text: The Congress of Vienna elevates Hanover from electorate to kingdom in 1814, recognizing its loyalty and sacrifice during the Napoleonic Wars.

advances.name: Hanoverian Constitution
advances.text: The Staatsgrundgesetz of 1833 establishes a constitutional framework for the Kingdom of Hanover, balancing royal prerogative with representative government.

advances.name: Clausthal Mining Academy
advances.text: The mining school at Clausthal applies modern science and engineering to the ancient Harz mines, pioneering industrial techniques that spread across German mining districts.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Welfs
destiny.text: The Brunswick-Luneburg lands are united under a single Welf banner. Whether we look westward across the sea or inward to the libraries of the Empire, our destiny awaits.

event.title: Destiny of the Welfs
event.text: The consolidation of Hanover marks a beginning, not an end. The House of Welf stands at a crossroads. To the west, the tides of the North Sea beckon: the British succession, maritime trade, and the power of a dual crown. To the south, the lecture halls of Gottingen and the libraries of the Empire offer a different kind of greatness: one built not on warships but on ideas. The path we choose now will define what Hanover becomes.

destiny.name: North Sea Coast
destiny.text: Secure control of Bremen and Oldenburg to command the Weser and Ems estuaries, giving Hanover direct access to the North Sea trade routes.

conditions.text: Own Bremen, or a subject owns it
Own Oldenburg, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Weser and the Ems
event.text: With Bremen and Oldenburg under our control, Hanover commands the estuaries of the Weser and the Ems. North Sea trade flows through our ports. The shipyards of Bremen build vessels that carry Hanoverian goods to Britain, the Netherlands, and beyond. This is the foundation upon which a maritime Hanover shall be built.

options.text: The North Sea is our highway

destiny.name: The British Crown
destiny.text: When the British crown looks abroad for a Protestant heir, the path to London opens to the Welfs. Bring the British crown under Welf rule and unite the two kingdoms across the North Sea. This stage cannot be completed before the Age of Reformation.

conditions.text: Own London, or a subject owns it

event.title: A Crown Across the Sea
event.text: The Welf dynasty wears the British crown. London, the greatest city in the world, acknowledges a Hanoverian monarch. The personal union brings immense opportunities: we may leverage the diplomatic weight of ruling two kingdoms to reshape the balance of power, or we may exploit the commercial networks of the North Sea to fill our treasury with trade revenue.

options.text: Two crowns, one dynasty: our diplomacy is supreme

modifiers.name: Royal Union
modifiers.text: The personal union of Hanover and Britain gives our diplomats unrivaled leverage in every court of Europe.

options.text: Two ports, one sea: our merchants shall prosper

modifiers.name: North Sea Commerce
modifiers.text: The merchant fleets of two kingdoms fill our harbors with the wealth of the North Sea trade.

destiny.name: North Sea Imperium
destiny.text: From Edinburgh to Amsterdam, the North Sea is a Hanoverian lake. Command its shores, its fleets, and its commerce.

conditions.text: Own Amsterdam, or a subject owns it
Own Edinburgh, or a subject owns it

event.title: Lords of the North Sea
event.text: From the harbors of Edinburgh to the counting houses of Amsterdam, the North Sea answers to Hanover. Our fleets patrol its waters, our merchants dominate its trade, our dynasty rules its greatest kingdoms. We may press our advantage at sea, building a true thalassocracy that challenges the old naval powers, or we may use our maritime wealth to anchor an unassailable position on the continent.

options.text: Command the waves: our navy shall rule the sea

modifiers.name: Hanoverian Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: Our warships command the North Sea, though the army suffers from neglect as resources flow to the dockyards.

options.text: Anchor the continent: our wealth secures our borders

modifiers.name: Continental Bastion
modifiers.text: Maritime wealth funds a mobile, well-supplied army that secures Hanover's position as the anchor of any continental coalition.

destiny.name: University Network
destiny.text: Begin a network of universities that will make Hanover the scholarly capital of the Empire. Take Erfurt and its venerable university, and raise Helmstedt into a town fit for the Welf university Duke Julius founded there.

conditions.text: Own Erfurt, or a subject owns it
Helmstedt is ours and has grown into a town

event.title: The Scholarly Network
event.text: With Erfurt's venerable university brought into the Hanoverian orbit and Helmstedt raised into a university town, the Gottingen model spreads. Our universities attract scholars from across the Empire: theologians, jurists, historians, and natural philosophers who debate freely in the tradition of Leibniz. Hanover is becoming synonymous with learning.

destiny.name: The Aufklarung
destiny.text: Gottingen's ideas are to travel across Germany. Build Gottingen into a university town of the first rank with a library to match, bring books into the scholarly market, and lead the German Enlightenment.

conditions.text: We own Göttingen and it has a Library
We own Göttingen and its development is at least 33

children.text: Books is produced in the market
Books is traded in the market

event.title: Light of the Aufklarung
event.text: The presses of Gottingen and Hanover pour forth books, pamphlets, and scholarly journals that reshape how Germans think about law, governance, and the natural world. Our universities are the intellectual engine of the Empire. We may push further toward secular scholarship, embracing religious tolerance and cosmopolitan learning, or we may channel this intellectual energy into systematic cameralist administration, making Hanover a model of rational governance.

modifiers.name: Secular Scholarship
modifiers.text: Our universities teach freely, unconstrained by confessional orthodoxy, though the religious establishment chafes at this tolerance.

modifiers.name: Cameralist State
modifiers.text: Systematic administration and fiscal discipline make Hanover a model of rational governance, though bureaucratic caution slows the path to war.

destiny.name: Beacon of Reason
destiny.text: Hanover stands as the intellectual beacon of Europe. Raise a Welf University in Gottingen, the Georgia Augusta, secure Leipzig's book trade, and build a society where reason and tolerance flourish.

conditions.text: We own Göttingen and a Welf University stands there
Own Leipzig, or a subject owns it

event.title: Beacon of Reason
event.text: Hanover stands as proof that a small German state can rival the great powers, not through conquest alone, but through the power of ideas. Our universities produce the finest scholars in Europe, our tolerance draws talent from every confession, our book trade carries the Aufklarung to every corner of the continent. We may build upon this intellectual network to project soft power and diplomatic influence, or we may harness the practical fruits of Enlightenment thought to build an industrialized, modern military state.

options.text: The pen is mightier: our ideas reshape Europe

modifiers.name: Republic of Letters
modifiers.text: Hanover's scholarly network spans the continent, giving our diplomats and statesmen an intellectual authority that few can match.

options.text: Knowledge applied, science serves the state

modifiers.name: Industrial Enlightenment
modifiers.text: The practical fruits of Aufklarung scholarship (chemistry, metallurgy, engineering) are channeled into building a modern, well-equipped military.

units.name: Subsidientruppen
units.text: Professional Hanoverian soldiers hired out to allied powers, well-drilled and dependable regulars who fight wherever their duke's treaties require.

units.name: Reisige
units.text: Armoured horsemen of the Welf dukes, drawn from the ducal household and the knightly families of the land. They are steady under fire and are kept for the decisive charge.

units.name: Hanoverian Redcoats
units.text: The red-coated regulars of the Elector-King, drilled to the same manual as the British foot beside whom they serve and tempered at Dettingen and in the long defence of the electorate.

units.name: Hanoverian Jager
units.text: Forest-bred riflemen from the woods of Lower Saxony, skilled in skirmishing, ambush, and making every shot count in broken terrain.

buildings.name: Oberharzer Bergwerk
buildings.text: A Harz Mountain silver mine equipped with the ingenious Wasserregal water management system: dams, ditches, and water wheels that power deep-shaft extraction.

where.text: Silver is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Sachsenspiegel Gericht
buildings.text: A law court administering justice according to the Sachsenspiegel: the foundational code of Saxon customary law that shaped legal practice across northern Germany.

buildings.name: Ducal Marstall
buildings.text: The stables and stud of a Welf court. Horses bred on the heath pastures are raised here for the duke's riders and for the plough, supplying the cavalry and enriching the rural economy.

buildings.name: Welf University
buildings.text: A university of the Welf lands, with a library open to its scholars and a press of its own, that draws students from across Europe and trains the councillors of the state.

buildings.name: Welf Residence
buildings.text: A moated castle rebuilt as a princely court: chapel, great hall and chancery around one yard, where the duke keeps his council, his painters and his singers.

buildings.name: Hanoverian Admiralty
buildings.text: A naval headquarters coordinating the combined maritime forces of Hanover's North Sea dominions, overseeing fleet construction, port defense, and trade convoy protection.

buildings.name: Akademie der Wissenschaften
buildings.text: A royal academy of sciences in the tradition of Leibniz, uniting natural philosophy, mathematics, and applied engineering under a single institution devoted to advancing human knowledge.

list.name: Geheimes Ratskollegium
list.text: The Hanoverian Privy Council, organised by the 1618 Regimentsordnung into specialised Ratsstuben: the Konsistorium for ecclesiastical affairs, the Kriegsrat for war, and the Haushaltsrat for finance. After the 1714 personal union the Geheimer Rat became the de-facto government of the Electorate, advising the absent prince through written memoranda transmitted via the Deutsche Kanzlei in London. It was the institutional spine of a state ruled in absentia by an elector-king who rarely visited his German lands.

list.name: Hannoversche Landstände
list.text: The territorial estates of the Calenberg-Lüneburg-Grubenhagen lands, organised in three curiae: the prelates of the secularised abbeys, the Ritterschaft of the country knights, and the deputies of the small Welf cities. The Landstände negotiated tax grants, supervised the Klosterfonds, and survived as a real bargaining counterweight to the absent elector. Hanover never produced the kind of absolutism Brandenburg-Prussia did: the 1714 Act of Settlement implicitly preserved the estates by binding the British crown not to wage Hanoverian wars without their consent.

list.name: Hannoversches Heer
list.text: The standing Hanoverian Army, raised by Ernest Augustus during the 1680s and made permanent after the 1692 elevation to electorate. The Heer fought at the Siege of Vienna in 1683 under the future George I, served in every Empire war from the Spanish Succession to the American Revolution, and, after the personal union, shared a monarch but never a treasury with the British Army. Recruitment ran by Werbung in the country districts, with cantonal levies that fell heavily on the peasantry in years of war.

list.name: Deutsche Kanzlei in London
list.text: The German Chancery, established by ordinance on 29 August 1714 to govern Hanover from London during the elector-king's absence. The Kanzlei was a small office of three Hanoverian ministers attached to the British court who transmitted memoranda between the Geheimer Rat at Hanover and the elector, and, crucially, kept Hanoverian foreign policy formally separate from British. Friction between the Kanzlei's German ministers and the elector's British advisors was constant, and the office became notorious in Westminster as the channel through which Hanoverian interests leaked into British policy.

list.name: Oberappellationsgericht zu Celle
list.text: The High Court of Appeal at Celle, established as the Cellesche Hofgericht in 1711 with Weipart Ludwig von Fabrice as its first president. The Oberappellationsgericht inherited the judicial chancery of the old Lüneburg-Celle ducal residence (1378-1705) and turned it into the highest civil court of the Welf lands. Its rulings on noble inheritance, manorial jurisdiction, and the rights of the Klöster were definitive across the Electorate, and the court continued to function under successor regimes long after the Hofgericht itself was reorganised into the Appellationshof in 1810.

list.name: Georgia Augusta zu Göttingen
list.text: The University of Göttingen, founded in 1734 by King George II of Great Britain on the urging of his Hanoverian first minister Gerlach Adolph von Münchhausen, with instruction beginning in 1737. Designed from the start as an Enlightenment university, the Georgia Augusta refused traditional confessional oaths, recruited Halle's Pietist law faculty, and made historical-critical scholarship and the natural sciences central to the curriculum. By the late 18th century it produced more Hanoverian civil servants than any other institution and trained the founders of modern German history (Schlözer and Heeren) and the physicist Lichtenberg.
